## TL;DR
`repoos restart` restarts this repo's server whether it is a RepoOS service, an external launchd/systemd supervisor, or hand-run. This round fixes the three pass-3 review findings: system-domain LaunchDaemons (the Kamrai case) are now detected, a RepoOS-managed unit is never signalled, and a pid is always verified before SIGTERM.

## Work and rationale
- `supervisor-detect.ts`: when non-root `launchctl list` has no row for the pid, the lookup now also reads `launchctl print system` and `launchctl print gui/<uid>` (both work without sudo) and maps pid to label. The Kamrai `org.repoos.serve.kamrai` daemon is therefore classified as `external`, and restart signals it so KeepAlive respawns it.
- New `managed` result kind for `com.repoos.serve.*` labels (launchd and systemd). `classifyRestartPath` refuses it with "use `repoos service restart`" when the service manager does not report it running, rather than falling through to hand-run and racing KeepAlive into a second server.
- `server-locate.ts` and `server-restart.ts`: `/api/health` carries no pid, so a pid is now always checked with `verifyPidServesRepo` before it is located or signalled.
- Tests: system-domain detection from `launchctl print system` output, managed kind, and refusal of an unverified pid even when health answers.
- Merged main; took main's copy of the task file and other tasks' bookkeeping.

## Approaches tried
Parsing `launchctl print system` with the same pid/status/label row parser as `launchctl list`; the services block uses the same columns so no second parser was needed. Reading the plist directly was rejected: the label is not enough to map to a running pid.

## Challenges and blockers
No real non-sudo KeepAlive LaunchDaemon was available to respawn-test; detection is covered by fixture output only.

## Key learnings
Non-root `launchctl list` only shows the caller's domain, so any supervisor detection must also consult the `system` domain. A pid-less health endpoint cannot authenticate a pid.
